beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the cancellation notice up the committee chart.
beats.text: The chair introduces difficult business. You tell them the trip is cancelled; I will take the minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You cancelled the trip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which makes me the author of the notice, not its authorized speaker.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my name under Secretary, leaving Chair blank.
beats.text: I have volunteered to record the difficult conversation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then who starts it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I push the blank Chair badge toward you.
beats.text: The highest-ranking person. Congratulations on your promotion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I decline?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. The deputy would then inherit the announcement. I have left that badge available too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold my coat and open a form headed Friendship Closure.
beats.text: Initial here to confirm we have made up. Then I can leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already said we were fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was verbal approval. We still need the written version to match the tone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I number the two empty teacups.
beats.text: We cannot end the visit until both parties approve the final tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I finished mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I refill my own cup.
beats.text: A refill reopens the procedure. Are we definitely okay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You are inventing rules to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let us record that understanding together before closing the visit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hide my glue-covered thumb behind an evidence clipboard.
beats.text: I will lead the broken-vase inquiry. Start by examining everyone who was outside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were alone with the vase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why I am best placed to decide which details matter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover my muddy footprint with a sign reading Investigation Headquarters.
beats.text: All evidence comes through me. Nobody moves this sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It is covering your boot print.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a second sign over my boot.
beats.text: An excellent clue. I am appointing myself evidence custodian.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can someone else examine it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once my office approves an independent review of my office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover the signature on the haunted copier invoice with a calculator.
beats.text: Fine, it prints prophecies. Before we discuss who ordered it, what is its maintenance budget?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your name is on the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then invoice me after we decide whether prophecy ink counts as a consumable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide my summoning note under the dragon feeding chart.
beats.text: Yes, there is a dragon in reception. Who is buying enough breakfast?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you summon it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I count the empty cereal boxes.
beats.text: We can discuss authorship after somebody takes the first feeding shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You keep changing the subject.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only toward the hungry part of it. Is there a bulk discount?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn my visitor badge facedown beside the closed folder.
beats.text: You can give me the insider version. Which account of last night have you heard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which account did you hear?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want to know whether we have the same clearance before comparing notes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pull up a chair at the private briefing.
beats.text: Start with the part everyone in this room knows.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tell us your part first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I open an empty notebook as though checking classified notes.
beats.text: I would hate to reveal something above your clearance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you actually cleared?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An excellent question. Which details would a cleared person already have?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the unopened result letter beside my medal.
beats.text: Read the first line for me. As a colleague, not as someone you feel sorry for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can read all of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One line. I am delegating a task, not surrendering my entire competence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide my ringing phone across and start polishing the medal.
beats.text: Take this call. Consider it a temporary exchange of professional duties.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You look upset.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set the polishing cloth down precisely.
beats.text: I look like someone assigning a phone call.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What can I tell them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That I will answer the hard part myself after a very competent minute.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I steady the single floating chair with both hands.
beats.text: This chair is everything. A flying chair needs a flying table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole house is floating.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The house can wait. Where does this chair put its breakfast?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tie a ribbon around the floating chair to mark it as essential.
beats.text: Nobody touches this. It will need a flying dining room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we tether the house first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I sketch a ceiling above the chair.
beats.text: Only if that gives my chair a stable sky.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now you want a sky?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A small one. Everything else can use the ordinary weather.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the teaspoon three times as you reach for your coat.
beats.text: We have not performed the proper goodbye. Hold the biscuit level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. Can I go now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the witness biscuit confirms it. I will fetch another plate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set two cups in a farewell circle.
beats.text: The guest leaves after the closing tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have finished mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I refill both cups solemnly.
beats.text: You finished before the farewell toast. We have to restart together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is there a short version?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. We should discuss which shortened ceremony would honour this visit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I remove the new worker’s nameplate and hold out my keyring.
beats.text: Give me the master key. You would miss too many locked cupboards without me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new worker needs access too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can ask me. That keeps the indispensable part of the job in place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I bring the only labelled spare-key box to my chair.
beats.text: Hand over the spare set. I know every lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could label another set.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I close the box.
beats.text: Labels cannot remember which doors stick when it rains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can write that down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the notebook as well. The institutional memory should remain together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move my name higher on the repair certificate while watching your face.
beats.text: Say who fixed it. Unless that sounds boastful; I can use smaller letters.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I choose a smaller pen.
beats.text: Good. Was that admiration or just factual accuracy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold up the certificate, then lower it when you blink.
beats.text: Could you introduce me as the person who solved this? Casually.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How casually?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I demonstrate an over-rehearsed shrug.
beats.text: With the amount of enthusiasm you think I merit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want me to choose the praise?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Purely for accuracy. I can adjust the shrug afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw an evacuation route around the empty food cupboard.
beats.text: Excellent, no supplies means we can practise total self-sufficiency immediately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only need groceries.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the emergency is wonderfully solvable. Take the torch and two shopping bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold up the broken emergency handle.
beats.text: Wonderful. We discovered this before a real disaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The alarm is ringing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I open my backup kit with a delighted gasp.
beats.text: An authentic practice opportunity! Use the spare exit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That one is locked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can test the full emergency plan at last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I sort every cup except one enormous pan.
beats.text: I have handled the ordinary cleaning. Who wants the special finishing assignment?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That pan needs scrubbing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I thought someone might enjoy finally being trusted with something important.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I polish the mop handle and present it like an award.
beats.text: I have prepared everything for our first floor-care specialist.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don’t you do it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to my completed chore list.
beats.text: Because I believe in giving other people opportunities I have already had twelve times.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does the specialist get anything?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My sincere relief, which you may interpret as enthusiastic support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the two accounts under Accident and Deliberate.
beats.text: The missing ten minutes could support either. Tell me what happened before the lights went out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was looking for the switch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That helps Accident. Which switch did you try first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the bag photograph from one theory to another.
beats.text: You said box before. Describe the handles without naming the container.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There were two straps.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cross out the box theory.
beats.text: Then the bag survives. Where did those straps leave marks?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You’ve changed your explanation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I would rather lose a theory than keep inventing support for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass you the chair’s badge but keep the appeals file.
beats.text: You’re chair now. Announce that I’m the final authority on appeals.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then who actually decides?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You decide. I decide which decisions stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand you the keys and put on a badge marked adviser.
beats.text: The place is yours. Just introduce me as the person whose advice cannot be ignored.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is that advice or an order?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Advice. You’re in charge of following it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And when I disagree?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We’ll announce how independently you requested a second opinion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the only door key beside a spare Deputy badge.
beats.text: No need to put me in charge. Take this badge and handle the assignment I prepared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Deputy to whom?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No grand titles needed. Bring the result to whoever still has the key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my smaller chair behind the large desk.
beats.text: You take the visible leadership seat. I will organize what you do from here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That sounds like working for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer the deputy badge with a modest smile.
beats.text: Only if you insist on naming a perfectly helpful arrangement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I change the assignment?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the revised version to me before announcing your independent decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep the morning mugs in their usual order and hand you the repaired tap handle.
beats.text: Test the replacement first. If it works, breakfast can proceed exactly as always.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Couldn’t we use bottled water?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That changes the kettle step. I’d rather risk your test than our entire routine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set the experimental fitting in the familiar teacup position.
beats.text: Try it once before I move anything else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It might leak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a towel under your cup, leaving mine untouched.
beats.text: Then we will learn whether the old order can survive the new part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why me first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone must remain available to preserve the original breakfast sequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand you my keys automatically, then pause over the invitation.
beats.text: What do I put after your name? My hands still seem to think you’re my person.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just put friend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Which friend gets handed my keys without either of us asking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I begin dialling your number while you stand beside me.
beats.text: I was going to ask you where we should sit at the wedding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can ask me now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I show the seating form.
beats.text: As what? I keep reaching for you before I know the label.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We don’t need a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me fill in the box without pretending you’re anybody else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pack an emergency box beside our optimistic route map.
beats.text: Help me plan the good outcome. I want something to hope for while preparing for the worst.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why pack for failure?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it won’t interrupt us if hope gets a chance to work. Draw one route that stays open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the celebration glasses inside a protective packing box.
beats.text: Let’s plan the toast before the answer arrives.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You think they’ll reject us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pad the glasses more carefully.
beats.text: I can expect bad news and still ask you to hope with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What should we toast?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The possibility I haven’t managed to pack away yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set water beside the unopened results and choose the chair by the door.
beats.text: I can talk about the first page today. Water first, then that page.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And the rest?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another day with another glass. One manageable piece is still honest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a tissue box between two chairs.
beats.text: I can listen to one difficult thing, then I need a walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You offered to help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I fill both water glasses.
beats.text: I still am. I’m making the help small enough that I can stay present.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we keep talking on the walk?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: About the same one thing. Fresh air isn’t permission to open every page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold the approval stamp just above the form, covering the cost.
beats.text: A quick yes and I can release this immediately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I should read the cost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I lower the stamp a fraction.
beats.text: Or we can complete this simple approval while the desk is still open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the release key beside the unsigned permission.
beats.text: Nod first. Then I can unlock the details.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The details should come first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the key away from the lock.
beats.text: That would leave the approval waiting in a very inconvenient place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why the hurry?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The stamp is ready, the key is ready, and only your yes is delaying such prepared paperwork.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the apology form between us and tap its empty date box.
beats.text: Is there anything you ought to write here before we continue?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What am I apologizing for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We haven’t reached the words yet. First put the date above the line where apologies count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide a pen beneath the heading I am.
beats.text: Finish that sentence. Carefully inside the box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I am confused.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the pen back a millimetre.
beats.text: That won’t validate. The correct sentence begins in the apology square.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you tell me what happened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once the box is properly opened. We can’t discuss the incident with invalid stationery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put last year’s repair bill beside your entry ticket.
beats.text: Give me the safer first turn this time. I keep paying when your risks go wrong.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That would cost me my advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then taking the loss would finally show whose side our shared budget is on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I block the expensive ramp with the invoice I paid.
beats.text: Choose the slower route for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could lose the race.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle my name on the bill.
beats.text: And I could keep my savings. I’m asking you to lose something on my behalf for once.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want proof I care?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something more measurable than handing me the next repair receipt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put our old picnic photo beside the one-way ticket.
beats.text: Choose the trip. Then I’ll know that smile meant goodbye, not a promise to return.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a happy photograph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It still is from your side. Your next choice tells me how to look at mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the same picnic photo toward the departure gate.
beats.text: Yesterday you said we’d always have this. Which version survives if you go?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can go and still care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave space beside the photograph.
beats.text: Then choose one thing you’ll come back for, so the picture isn’t only a farewell.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want to change the memory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want your next act to stop changing it for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the key you gave me beside the locked drawer.
beats.text: Yesterday this meant welcome. Today I need the original note inside that drawer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You think I hid it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I don’t know. Hand me the note so this key can become a gift again instead of evidence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out the gifted key without returning it.
beats.text: Open the drawer and show me the letter itself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My account isn’t enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the key on an empty evidence envelope.
beats.text: Not while your welcome also gave me access to the missing page.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you accusing me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I’m asking for the proof that lets me pick the key up differently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I repeat our old greeting while holding the last teacup.
beats.text: Make yourself at home. I used to mean take off your shoes; today I mean don’t leave yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you needed the cup back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I needed a sentence that could bring you through the door. The cup was easier to ask for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the spare key beside a clean cup.
beats.text: When I said the door is always open, I meant I’d like you to use it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you wanted the key returned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I push it back toward you.
beats.text: That was the first reason I could say aloud.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What is the reason now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Make yourself at home. This time I’m not hiding the invitation inside a borrowed key.
